note: How Archer realizes the abstract language in ../../../patterns/index.json. Entries are keyed by `pattern` — an abstract id (`confirm`), a variant (`choose.segmented`) or a part (`screen#header`) — and every field means what docs/patterns-v2.md says it means. The reach-for table in patterns.md is generated from this file and the abstract one: run `npm run patterns-doc` in engine/ after editing either. Archer's parts are flat sibling exports off one import (`DialogPopup`, not `Dialog.Popup`), so a signature is written in those names. Two kinds of entry live here and they do different jobs. **Anatomy entries** record a shape the library *requires* — a Dialog is a root, a trigger, a popup and a title, in every file that has one. They exist so `patterns/unregistered-composite` does not report a component's own mandatory anatomy as house style nobody wrote down; each carries `canonical` set to the root import, so any file actually using the component is skipped before either composite rule sees it, and they therefore never produce a finding. **Judgement entries** record a composite that has a right and a wrong form; those carry `instead_of` and, where the wrong form is a recognisable composite in its own right, `instead_of_signature`. Most do not — the shape reached for by default is usually one control, and a rule that fires on every `Select` is a rule people turn off, which is why reading this file before assembling matters more than the check does. Archer ships a page header (`PageHeader`) and an empty state (`Empty`), and those entries name them as `canonical`. It ships no detail sidebar or settings drilldown: those entries are here without `canonical` on purpose, so the first project that builds one extracts it and fills that in rather than rebuilding it per screen. `AppShell` and `PageHeader` take their regions as props (`nav`, `actions`, `breadcrumb`), which a signature does not see, so neither has an anatomy entry: what a file puts inside them is the page, not their structure.

modal.note: Its anatomy is screen.overlay. A destructive confirmation is AlertDialog — see confirm.

menu.note: Commands, navigation destinations and in-menu settings. Its anatomy is action-cluster.overflow.

realizations.note: A segmented control: one value shared across a set of toggles.
Choosing one of a few options that should all stay visible.
Choosing one predefined value.
A value chosen from a filterable list.
Free-form text with suggestions. If the value must come from the list, that is Combobox (choose.combobox).

instead_of: A Stack holding a <label> above an Input, with the error message conditionally rendered beside it — Field owns the association, the aria wiring and the rhythm
A placeholder standing in for a label
realizations.note: A labelled control with its description and validation message, for any input that needs more than a placeholder.
Editing something already on screen, or a flow a Dialog would cramp.

instead_of: One-off panel layouts, each with its own width, padding and section rhythm
realizations.note: Not shipped: a panel of properties beside a main region, for inspecting or editing the selected thing without leaving the view. `Stack` plus `Separator` plus `Field` is the raw material; extract the composition once two exist.

instead_of: A div with hand-set margins between the buttons
Buttons spaced with margin-right
realizations.note: Two or three actions sitting together, primary last: the foot of a dialog, the end of a form, the corner of a header. Documentation, not a check — `Stack(Button,Button)` is a true description of an action bar and matches half of any codebase. There is no canonical: two buttons in a Stack with a gap is already the whole implementation. Reach for action-cluster.toolbar instead once there are groups or more than about four controls.

instead_of: A Stack of Buttons with a Separator between the groups — it looks the same and has no roving focus, so every control is a tab stop
realizations.note: A roving-focus bar of actions, grouped and separated: an action bar with more than a couple of controls, especially one with groups. A plain `Button` inside a `Toolbar` is the same defect one level down: it drops out of the roving-focus order. Use `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarLink` or `ToolbarInput`.

instead_of: Three secondary Buttons sitting in the header, competing with the one action that matters
realizations.note: Secondary actions on a thing — rename, duplicate, delete — on a row, card or header with more actions than deserve their own button. The signature is Menu's own anatomy, which also carries navigation destinations and in-menu settings.

instead_of: A Dialog with a title, a description and a Cancel/Confirm button pair — AlertDialog already is that, with the dismissal behaviour and button emphasis a destructive action needs
window.confirm()
realizations.note: Destructive or irreversible confirmation. The anti-shape is deliberately prose rather than an `instead_of_signature`: a form dialog also carries a title, a description and two buttons, and containment matching cannot tell the two apart. Decide this when you reach for the component, not from a finding.

instead_of: Tabs standing in for hierarchy
One long panel showing every control at once
A Select that swaps the pane beneath it
realizations.note: Not shipped: rows that open a further screen, rather than a wall of controls, for settings more than one level deep. Worth building rather than flattening: depth beats breadth, and a leaf screen that shows only what is actually set is far shorter than the panel it replaces.

instead_of: Tabs standing in for hierarchy — peers belong in tabs, depth belongs in navigation
realizations.note: Peer views of one subject.
Site or app navigation with rich panels.

instead_of: A Grid or a Stack of rows standing in for a table — it looks the same and is not navigable cell by cell
realizations.note: Tabular data. Archer ships the table, not a data view, so this is the items part and not browse-collection.list: sorting, filtering and pagination are the project's.

instead_of: An Accordion holding a single section
realizations.note: One expandable region. `Collapsible(CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsiblePanel)` is under the four-node floor, so the import is the check.

instead_of: An Accordion holding a single section — that is Collapsible
realizations.note: Several independently expandable sections.
Anchored, non-modal, interactive content.

instead_of: A bare 'No results' string where the rows would be
A spinner that never resolves because there is nothing to load
realizations.note: What a list, table or panel shows when it holds nothing yet, for any collection that can legitimately be empty. `Empty` takes `title`, `description` and a decorative `icon`; its `children` are the way out, usually one `Button`. An empty state is a finished, correct result — a failure is an `Alert`, and a wait is a `Spinner` or `Skeleton`.

instead_of: A hand-managed array of messages in component state, rendered into a fixed-position Stack — the manager already owns queueing, timing, focus and dismissal
An inline error rendered where the button was
realizations.note: Transient messages raised from anywhere in the app, for anything reporting the result of an action the user has already left behind. Mount `ToastProvider` once at the app root and raise from `useToastManager()`. There is nothing to compose, which is why this entry carries no signature.
A bulleted or numbered list.

instead_of: An ad-hoc row rebuilt per screen — a Stack holding a Heading, a Text and a Stack of Buttons — each with its own heading level and spacing
realizations.note: Screen title, optional description, and a trailing action cluster, at the top of any screen or pane. `PageHeader` takes `title`, `level` (1 for a screen, 2 for a pane), `description`, `breadcrumb` and `actions` as props, and its `children` are the row under the title — a `TabsList` or a horizontal `NavigationMenu`. The title is already a `Heading` with `variant="ui"`, so do not pass one in. The anti-shape stays prose: a Card or a Dialog also holds a Heading beside a Stack of Buttons, and containment matching cannot tell those apart from a hand-built header.
The trail of pages above the current one, usually passed to `PageHeader`'s `breadcrumb`.
Every modal task. Recorded so the required anatomy is not reported as an unregistered composite. Dialog is the container a form dialog is built in, not a shipped edit-record.dialog.
